title: Why Barry Marshall Swallowed Bacteria
topic: Why Barry Marshall drank a cup of bacteria in 1984

lines: A determined doctor gulped a cup of living bacteria.
Colleagues scoffed, saying no germ could survive the stomach’s acid.
Three days later nausea and terrible breath appear.
By day eight his stomach vomits without acid.
You see, it feels like swallowing a spoonful of fire and waiting for the burn.
The real reason: H. pylori’s urease neutralizes stomach acid, letting it colonise and cause acute gastritis.
His self‑infection proved Koch’s postulates and forced medicine to admit ulcers are infections, not just stress.

claims.claim: Marshall drank a broth containing cultured H. pylori in 1984 and soon developed nausea, bad breath, achlorhydric vomiting and gastritis.
H. pylori produces urease, which breaks down urea into ammonia and bicarbonate, raising pH and allowing the bacteria to survive in the stomach.
Marshall’s experiment fulfilled Koch’s postulates for H. pylori causing gastritis, overturning the belief that ulcers were caused by stress or acid alone.
